takeaways.label: Best quarter in IGI's history
takeaways.text: Highest-ever volumes, revenue, EBITDA and profits, with H1 revenue growing 27% and EBITDA 34%, well ahead of the 15%/20% guidance set in May.

takeaways.label: Lab-grown is the growth engine, natural is resilient
takeaways.text: LGD loose certification grew 37% and jewelry certification 47%, while natural diamond certification grew 8% despite a soft natural market.

takeaways.label: Full-year guidance upgraded, no specific number given
takeaways.text: Management expects H2 to deliver growth similar to H1, but repeatedly declined to pin down a revised percentage target when pressed.

takeaways.label: India margins dipped on deliberate investment
takeaways.text: Standalone EBITDA margin fell 340 bps to 69.5% as the company spent on leadership, marketing and commissions; consolidated margins expanded on operating leverage.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the lab-grown supply ramp continues converting into certification volumes at the same pace, how natural diamond momentum holds through the festive season, and any color on when India margin investments start paying back.

sections.title: Lab-Grown Diamond: Supply, Demand & IGI's Role

points.label: Supply ramp is structural, not cyclical
points.text: Large Indian growers are adding reactors and doubling capacity over three years; management sees supply at its base, not its peak, and expects no slowdown in LGD business for coming quarters.

points.label: Retail adoption broadening fast
points.text: In India, lab-grown chains are opening stores and established jewelers have launched LGD brands; in the US, more than 50% of all bridals are now lab-grown. LGD jewelry certification grew 47% in Q2 and 46% in H1, with consistency across quarters.

points.label: New geographies opening
points.text: Markets for LGD jewelry are expanding into Europe, Latin America and Australia, a trend management expects to continue.

points.label: LGD revenue stable quarter-on-quarter
points.text: Consolidated LGD revenue was ₹211.1 crore in Q2, essentially flat vs ₹209.5 crore in Q1, as scale-up from grower capacity additions flows into laboratories for certification.

points.label: First-time diamond buyers as a future natural-diamond pipeline
points.text: For many families, a lab-grown diamond is the very first diamond they buy; as household income rises they buy more pieces, bigger stones, and over coming years will move to natural diamonds.

points.label: IGI's certificate as the market's backbone
points.text: Management argues the IGI certificate is what makes a lab-grown diamond a diamond and protects natural diamond value, positioning the company as the independent standard a market of this size needs.

quotes.text: Printer: "It is the IGI certificate that makes the lab-grown diamond a diamond, and it is the same certificate that also protects the value of a natural diamond."

points.label: Growth despite a soft natural market
points.text: Natural diamond certification grew 8% YoY in Q2 and 5% sequentially, with H1 up 7% after a slow start to the year; traction is building.

points.label: Natural jewelry certification lagged
points.text: Grew only 3% in Q2, as high and volatile gold prices made buyers of natural diamond jewelry take longer to decide.

points.label: Momentum expected to hold
points.text: Management expects the natural diamond momentum to continue into the next two quarters.

points.label: Consolidated margin expansion
points.text: Q2 EBITDA margin reached 61.4%, up from 60.4% in Q1 and 60.1% in FY25-26, as operating leverage translated EBITDA growth faster than revenue growth.

points.label: India standalone margin compression
points.text: EBITDA margin fell 340 bps YoY (69.5% vs 72.8%), driven by investments in employee leadership, additional marketing and commission expenses. H1 PAT margins also dropped 340 bps on the same investments.

points.label: ARP drivers
points.text: India standalone ARP rose 7% driven by increased mix of LGD stones (up 6%); base business ARP grew 2% on higher LGD loose stone mix. Consolidated ARP rose 4% YoY, split evenly between AGL consolidation and base business LGD mix shift.

points.label: ARP sequential decline is seasonal
points.text: ARP fell 12% QoQ because LGD loose stones mix was 4% lower and jewelry mix was up ~3-4%, a normal seasonal pattern entering the festive Q2/Q3 period.

points.label: Overseas subsidiaries profitable
points.text: Overseas certification revenues grew 31% without AGL, and the business is increasingly profitable.

points.label: Operating leverage trend expected to persist
points.text: Management expects EBITDA growth to continue outpacing revenue growth.

points.label: First-mover advantage in LGD certification
points.text: IGI was the first to certify lab-grown diamonds, establishing trust and acceptance over 50 years.

points.label: The 4Cs as an enduring commercial standard
points.text: Management argues the 4Cs establish the commercial value at which goods trade across the value chain and will not go away.

points.label: Stance on lab-grown as a diamond
points.text: IGI is the only laboratory in the world to acknowledge lab-grown as a diamond, refusing to "lesser" it to something mundane; management sees this as a defining differentiator.

quotes.text: Printer: "We are the only laboratory in the world to acknowledge it as a diamond because both are exactly the same and natural diamond is earth-mined, laboratory diamond is man-made but both are diamonds... We will not lesser the diamond, like lab-grown, to something which is mundane."

points.label: Geographic expansion underway
points.text: Started operations in Italy this year, venturing into Saudi Arabia, and set up a company in Botswana in September.

points.label: AGL integration and global push
points.text: AGL has been part of IGI Group since January; colored stone capabilities are being built in other laboratories using AGL methods, and AGL itself is ready for a growth charter and expansion into key gemstone markets.

points.label: AI in laboratory operations
points.text: AI-based work allocations and scheduling are now in use, enabling the same team to grade more stones more efficiently and faster while keeping grading standards constant.

points.label: Brand investment scaling
points.text: Brand research volume for IGI is up 66% since March 2026; the company is reaching 2 crore unique audience every quarter consistently and has clocked 15 crore+ views on campaigns year-to-date. Capabilities are being built for regional content and strategy within India and across key global geographies.

points.label: Capital allocation priorities unchanged
points.text: Invest in capacities, geographies, and technology, selective bolt-on acquisitions, and return surplus cash; the Board reviews with each set of results.

items.title: FY27 guidance raised
items.text: After H1 FY27 revenue grew 27% and EBITDA 34%, management revised its original 15%/20% guidance upward and expects H2 growth rates similar to H1, with group EBITDA margin improving at least 100 bps by end-FY27. Operating leverage on a debt-free, 61% EBITDA-margin base means most incremental revenue drops to profit.

items.title: Lab-grown diamond certification
items.text: IGI holds 65% global LGD certification share, with consolidated LGD loose volumes up 37% YoY in Q2 FY27 and jewelry up 47%, as Indian CVD reactor count doubled to ~13-14k and large growers add capacity over three years. Retail is following supply - 1,000+ dedicated LGD outlets in India, $90M raised by LGD brands in 12 months, and over 50% of US bridals now lab-grown - each stone needing a certificate.

items.title: AGL coloured gemstone expansion
items.text: IGI completed the $13.2M acquisition of AGL (New York coloured gemstone lab) on 14 February 2026; gemstone certification revenue grew 331% YoY in Q2 FY27 to 6.3% of mix, with AGL adding 3% to H1 revenue growth. AGL methods are being rolled out to other IGI labs and collection windows starting in Jaipur, extending a small base into a new global vertical.

items.title: Natural diamond share gains
items.text: Natural loose certification grew 8% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 7% in H1 against a flat natural market, with international growth in double digits for three straight quarters. A dedicated natural vertical under a new business leader is pushing share of wallet from a ~50%+ India share, and management expects the momentum to continue into the next two quarters.

items.title: New-country expansion
items.text: Operations started in Italy in FY27, a Saudi subsidiary was approved in February 2026, a Botswana entity was set up in September 2026, and Dubai and Turkey are scaling; overseas lab revenue grew 31% in Q2 FY27 excluding AGL and is increasingly profitable. FY26 also added labs in Zhuji (the pearl hub), Jaipur, Lucknow, Raipur and Dubai's Deira Gold Souk, taking the network to 36 labs in 10 countries.

items.title: US market build-out
items.text: New US sales leadership is in place and the commercial team expanded, with early traction including the first Origin screening sale, a JewelPass launch, and a screening programme covering 100,000+ pieces for one of the largest US jewelry retailers. With 70-80% of US loose diamonds certified in India, deeper US penetration targets a $50-70B retail diamond jewelry market.

items.title: India Tier 2/3 and grader capacity
items.text: New labs in Lucknow, Raipur and a second Jaipur site extend reach into cities with lower certification awareness, supported by another round of large grader recruitment to hold turnaround times as volumes grow. India certification revenue grew 28% in Q2 FY27 on 19% volume growth at a 69.5% EBITDA margin, with margins expected to stabilise around 70%.
